en: to be scheduled; to be planned

examples.en: The new drama was scheduled for Friday night.

examples.ko: 내년 예산이 교육에 많이 편성돼 있어요.
examples.en: A large share of next year's budget is allocated to education.
The team was newly formed, so it felt awkward at first.
Once the timetable is arranged, I'll tell the students.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 아침 시간대로 편성될 거예요.
examples.en: This program will be slotted into the morning.
The classes were organized by level, so the lessons became easier.

explain: 방송 시간표, 예산, 팀, 반처럼 여러 요소를 짜서 정리할 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '예산이 편성되다'가 가장 자주 나와요. 일정이 그냥 정해지는 '정해지다'보다 틀을 짠다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The broadcaster schedules the new program in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편성하다는 짜는 쪽, 편성되다는 짜인 결과 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '편성하다' is from the side arranging; '편성되다' is from the side of the result.

phrases.en: A budget was set up for the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 자주 나오는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use in the news.

phrases.en: I checked the broadcast schedule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송 프로그램의 시간과 순서를 정리한 표를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A table listing the times and order of broadcast programs.

explain_en: Use it when several elements are arranged into a plan, such as a broadcast schedule, a budget, a team or a class. In the news, '예산이 편성되다' (a budget is drawn up) is the most common. Compared with '정해지다' (to be decided), it feels like a framework is being put together.

t90.ax: The new drama was scheduled for Friday night.

en: to play a role; to play a part

examples.en: That song played a part in the drama's popularity.
The good weather also plays a role in the festival's success.

examples.ko: 친구의 응원이 합격에 한몫한 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think my friend's encouragement helped me pass.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 편리해서 인기를 얻는 데 한몫하고 있어요.
examples.en: This app is convenient, which is helping it become popular.

examples.ko: 가격이 싼 것도 한몫하겠지만 품질이 더 중요해요.
examples.en: The low price will play a part too, but quality is more important.

examples.ko: 당신도 이번 일에 한몫했으니 같이 축하해요.
examples.en: You played a part in this too, so let's celebrate together.

explain: 'N이/가 ~에 한몫하다'처럼 어떤 일에 도움이 되거나 영향을 준 몫이 크다고 말할 때 써요. 좋은 결과에 많이 쓰지만 나쁜 결과에도 쓸 수 있어요. '한몫 잡다'처럼 큰 이익을 얻는 뜻의 표현과는 쓰임이 달라요.

phrases.en: My friend's encouragement played a big role.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한몫하다'와 뜻이 비슷하고 더 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 한몫하다 and used more widely.

phrases.example: 새 광고가 매출 증가에 톡톡히 한몫했어요.
phrases.en: The new ad played a solid part in the sales increase.
phrases.nuance_ko: '톡톡히'를 붙이면 몫이 꽤 컸다는 뜻이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 톡톡히 stresses that the contribution was substantial.

phrases.en: Steady effort played a part in his success.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에 한몫하다' 꼴로, 무엇에 도움이 됐는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the form '~에 한몫하다', used to say what something contributed to.
phrases.en_equiv: to play a part in success

explain_en: It is used as 'N이/가 ~에 한몫하다' to say something contributed a good share to a result. It is often used for good outcomes but can also be used for bad ones. It is different from '한몫 잡다', which means making a big profit.

examples.en: This tool has many uses.
I chose a bag to suit how I'd use it.
I decided to clear out things that have no use.
We learn how this word is used through example sentences.
I found a new use for the discarded bottle.
I write down where my money goes in a household ledger.

explain: '쓰임새가 많다/적다/있다/없다', '쓰임새를 찾다'처럼 써요. '용도'는 정해진 목적이고, '쓰임새'는 실제로 어디에 어떻게 쓰이는지를 말해서 더 쉽고 부드러워요. 돈의 쓰임새는 쓰는 곳, 말의 쓰임새는 쓰는 방법과 상황이에요.

phrases.example: 이 상자는 쓰임새가 많아서 자주 써요.
phrases.en: This box has many uses, so I use it often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 물건을 여러 가지로 쓸 수 있을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used when one thing can be used in many ways.

phrases.en: This thing had no use, so I threw it away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸 데가 없다는 뜻이고 '쓰임새가 많다'의 반대예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means there is nothing to use it for; the opposite of 쓰임새가 많다.

phrases.en: I'm looking for a use for the leftover cloth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금은 쓸 데가 없는 물건을 어디에 쓸지 생각할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when thinking about what to do with something that has no current use.

explain_en: You say '쓰임새가 많다/적다/있다/없다' and '쓰임새를 찾다'. '용도' is the fixed purpose, while '쓰임새' is about how and where something actually gets used, and it sounds easier and softer. The '쓰임새' of money is where it is spent; of a word, how and in what situations it is used.

dis.h: how and where it is used; versatility

p.n: 용도 stresses the purposes it serves. 쓰임새 stresses how it is used.

examples.en: Experts estimate that the damage is large.
It's hard to estimate the exact age.

examples.ko: 경찰은 사고 시간을 밤 열 시쯤으로 추정했어요.
examples.en: The police estimated the accident happened around ten at night.

examples.ko: 값을 추정할 때는 비슷한 물건과 비교해요.
examples.en: When I estimate a price, I compare it with similar items.

examples.ko: 자료를 보면 손님이 늘 것으로 추정돼요.
examples.en: The data suggests that customers will increase.
What's your reason for presuming that?

explain: '짐작하다'는 가볍게 생각해 보는 거고, 추정하다는 자료나 근거로 계산하거나 판단한다는 느낌이 강해요. 뉴스에서 숫자와 함께 '~로 추정돼요'를 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '아마 ~일 것 같아요'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 이 자료로 대략의 숫자를 추정할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: We can estimate a rough number from this data.
phrases.nuance_ko: 근거가 있어서 판단이 가능하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a judgment is possible because there is evidence.

phrases.en: I made a rough estimate of the number of spectators.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정확한 값이 아니라 어림잡아 계산한다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the sense of an approximate figure rather than an exact one.

phrases.en: I guessed the mood from the look on their face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '추정하다'보다 가볍고, 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter than 추정하다 and more common in daily conversation.

explain_en: '짐작하다' is a casual guess, while 추정하다 suggests judging from data or evidence. News often says '~로 추정돼요' next to numbers. In daily talk, '아마 ~일 것 같아요' sounds more natural.

dis.h: estimate or presume from evidence, formal

p.n: 짐작하다 is a gut guess; 추정하다 is a judgment based on evidence.

t90.ax: It's hard to estimate the exact age.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 템포가 빨라서 춤추기 좋아요.
examples.en: This song has a fast tempo, so it's great for dancing.
The pace of the work is so slow that it's frustrating.
Try slowing down the pace of your presentation a little.
If we can't keep the tempo, the choir falls apart.
The drama moved at a quick pace, so it wasn't boring.
A slow walking pace is comfortable for me.

explain: 음악뿐 아니라 일, 말, 이야기가 진행되는 빠르기에도 써요. 자동차나 달리기의 빠르기는 '속도'라고 하고, 템포는 흐름의 빠르기를 말할 때 어울려요. '템포가 빠르다/느리다'로 써요.

phrases.en: This movie has a slow pace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기나 진행이 느릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a story or process moves slowly.

phrases.en: It was too hard, so I slowed my running pace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르기를 일부러 줄일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you deliberately reduce the speed.

phrases.example: 빠른 템포의 음악을 들으면 힘이 나요.
phrases.en: Listening to fast-tempo music gives me energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악이나 흐름이 빠를 때 '빠른'을 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 빠른 in front for fast music or flow.

explain_en: Besides music, 템포 is used for how fast work, speech, or a story moves. For the speed of a car or a runner you say 속도; 템포 fits the speed of a flow. It goes with 템포가 빠르다/느리다.

examples.ko: 저는 하루 필요량보다 물을 적게 마시고 있어요.
examples.en: I am drinking less water than the amount I need per day.

examples.ko: 아이에게 필요한 영양소의 필요량은 나이마다 달라요.
examples.en: The amount of nutrients a child needs differs by age.
I buy only what I need, so I don't throw food away.
I calculated the amount needed and ordered the ingredients.

examples.ko: 비타민 하루 필요량은 음식으로도 채울 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can also meet the daily vitamin requirement through food.

examples.ko: 운동을 많이 하면 단백질 필요량이 늘어요.
examples.en: If you exercise a lot, your protein requirement increases.

explain: 영양, 물, 전기, 재료처럼 숫자로 잴 수 있는 것에 '이만큼 필요하다'고 말할 때 써요. '하루 필요량'처럼 앞에 기간을 붙이는 경우가 많아요. 짝말은 '충분하다/부족하다'예요.

phrases.en: I drink as much water as I need per day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하루 동안 꼭 필요한 양을 말할 때 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for the amount needed in one day.

phrases.example: 물을 필요량보다 적게 마셔서 자주 목이 말라요.
phrases.en: I drink less water than I need, so I often feel thirsty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 먹거나 쓴 양이 필요한 양에 못 미칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount actually taken or used falls short of what is needed.

phrases.example: 하루에 물 두 리터로 필요량을 채워요.
phrases.en: I meet my need with two liters of water a day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 양만큼 다 먹거나 모았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you took or gathered the full amount required.

explain_en: Use it for measurable things such as nutrients, water, electricity or materials when saying how much is needed. A period often comes before it, as in '하루 필요량' (daily requirement). It pairs with '충분하다' (enough) and '부족하다' (short).

examples.en: The new factory starts operating next week.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 배수 장치가 자동으로 가동됐어요.
examples.en: When the rain started, the drainage system switched on automatically.

examples.ko: 정상적으로 가동되는 기계는 한 대밖에 없어요.
examples.en: Only one machine is running normally.

examples.ko: 전기가 들어오면 모든 장비가 가동될 거예요.
examples.en: When the power comes in, all the equipment will start running.
As the power plant went into operation, the nearby villages became brighter.

examples.ko: 비상 시스템이 가동되어서 모두 안전하게 나왔어요.
examples.en: The emergency system kicked in, and everyone got out safely.

explain: 공장, 기계, 발전소, 시스템처럼 움직이는 설비가 작동하기 시작하거나 돌아가고 있을 때 써요. 사람이 쓰는 도구에는 잘 안 써요. 멈추면 '중단되다', 사람이 켜면 '가동하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The factory is running normally.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제 없이 잘 돌아간다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is running without problems.

phrases.en: The repair finished and the machine was running again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멈췄던 것이 다시 움직일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something that stopped starts running again.

phrases.en: The power plant is running now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 돌아가고 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of currently running.

explain_en: Used when equipment such as a factory, machine, power plant or system starts working or is running. It isn't used for hand tools. When it stops, it's 중단되다, and when someone starts it, the active verb is 가동하다.

en: to slow down; to become dull

examples.en: Economic growth is gradually slowing down.

examples.ko: 나이가 들면 몸의 신진대사가 점점 둔화돼요.
examples.en: As you get older, your body's metabolism gradually slows down.

examples.ko: 수출 증가세가 둔화된 이유를 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: Please explain why export growth has slowed.

examples.ko: 올해 안에 소비가 둔화될 가능성이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a possibility that spending will slow down within this year.

examples.ko: 추운 날씨에는 근육의 움직임이 둔화되기 쉬워요.
examples.en: In cold weather, muscle movement easily becomes sluggish.
If your reaction speed slows, driving is dangerous.

explain: 속도나 활동이 점점 느려지거나 무뎌질 때 써요. 경제뿐 아니라 몸의 반응, 감각에도 쓸 수 있어요. 반대로 빨라질 때는 '가속화되다'라고 해요. 쉽게는 '느려지다', '둔해지다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: Growth appears likely to slow down next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 전망을 말할 때 쓰는 뉴스식 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style expression for stating a forecast.

phrases.en: The pace of economic growth slowed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '둔화되다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 둔화되다 and more common in daily conversation.

phrases.en: Your senses become duller as you age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 반응이나 감각이 무뎌질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when body reactions or senses become dull.

explain_en: It is used when speed or activity gradually slows or dulls. Besides the economy, it also applies to body reactions and senses. The opposite is '가속화되다'. In simpler words people say '느려지다' or '둔해지다'.

en: to be changed; to be altered

examples.en: The meeting time was changed.
I got a text saying my password was changed.
The schedule might change suddenly.
Please send it to the updated address.
The reservation wasn't changed.
The rule changed, so I'll explain it again.

explain: 일정, 시간, 주소처럼 정해진 내용이 다른 것으로 바뀔 때 써요. 공지나 문자에서 자주 봐요. 자연스럽게 모습이 달라지는 변화에는 '변하다'를 쓰고, 이 말은 정한 것을 바꾼다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I'll let you know the changed time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바뀐 내용을 안내할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to announce updated details.

phrases.en: The schedule may change.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바뀔 가능성이 있다고 미리 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to warn in advance that something might change.

phrases.en: My address hasn't changed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그대로라고 확인해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to confirm that something stayed the same.

explain_en: Used when a fixed detail such as a schedule, time or address is switched to something else. You often see it in notices and text messages. For a natural change in appearance or state, a different verb is used, while this one suggests a set arrangement was altered.

dis.h: formal; a plan or setting is officially altered
gh: everyday; something becomes different or switches
stiff; a state or situation changes gradually

examples.en: The screen suddenly switches to a different scene.
This semester's classes were switched to online.

examples.ko: 회의 분위기가 밝게 전환되자 모두 웃었어요.
examples.en: Once the mood of the meeting turned brighter, everyone laughed.
The pace of the switch to electric cars is getting faster.
I was worried the situation would turn against us.

examples.ko: 휴대폰이 무음 모드로 전환된 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I did not know the phone had switched to silent mode.

explain: 상태, 방식, 방향이 다른 것으로 바뀔 때 써요. '온라인으로 전환되다', '분위기가 전환되다'처럼 말해요. '바뀌다'보다 딱딱하고 큰 변화에 어울려요. 기분을 바꾼다는 '기분 전환'도 같은 한자어예요.

phrases.en: Thanks to the joke, the mood changed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분위기나 방향이 다른 쪽으로 바뀔 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for a mood or direction shifting.

phrases.en: Classes are switching to online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 바뀌는 중이라는 진행을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that the change is in progress.

phrases.en: The plan changed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 변화에도 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple word that also works for small changes.

explain_en: Use it when a state, method or direction changes into another, as in '온라인으로 전환되다' or '분위기가 전환되다'. It is more formal than '바뀌다' and fits bigger changes. '기분 전환' (a change of mood) uses the same word.

t90.ax: This semester's classes were switched to online.

examples.en: Words are combined and new words are formed.
Consonants and vowels are put together to make a letter.

examples.ko: 여러 재료가 조합된 샌드위치가 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: The sandwich that combines several ingredients is very popular.

examples.ko: 색깔이 어떻게 조합되느냐에 따라 느낌이 달라요.
examples.en: The feel changes depending on how the colors are combined.

examples.ko: 숫자 네 개가 조합되면 비밀번호가 돼요.
examples.en: When four numbers are put together, they make a password.

examples.ko: 좋은 팀은 서로 다른 장점이 잘 조합되어 있어요.
examples.en: In a good team, different strengths are well combined.

explain: '조합하다'는 사람이 짜 맞추는 쪽이고, '조합되다'는 여럿이 합쳐져 하나가 된 결과를 말해요. 글자, 색, 재료, 숫자처럼 부분이 여러 개일 때 써요. 그냥 섞이는 '섞이다'보다 짜임새가 있는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 여러 재료가 조합되어 새로운 맛이 나요.
phrases.en: Several ingredients combine to make a new taste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부분이 여러 개일 때 쓰는 대표적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical use when there are several parts.

phrases.example: 이 비밀번호는 숫자와 글자가 조합되어 있어요.
phrases.en: This password is a combination of numbers and letters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 합쳐진 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where things are already combined.
phrases.en_equiv: is made up of a combination

phrases.en: I combine colors well when I get dressed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 직접 짜 맞출 때 쓰는 능동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, used when a person puts things together.

explain_en: '조합하다' is when a person puts parts together; '조합되다' describes the result of several parts forming one whole. Use it when there are several components, such as letters, colors, ingredients or numbers. Compared with '섞이다' (to mix), it feels more structured.

examples.en: This machine is used for smoke detection.
I took a lie detector test.
The radar's detection range has widened.
It's a disease where early detection is important.
They turned off the signal to avoid detection.
At the airport they do explosive detection training.

explain: '발견'은 찾아내서 알게 되는 일 전반이고, '탐지'는 기계나 도구를 써서 숨어 있는 것을 일부러 찾아내는 일이에요. 그래서 '연기 탐지', '금속 탐지', '거짓말 탐지'처럼 기계 이름과 함께 자주 나와요. 일상 대화보다는 뉴스, 기술, 과학 글에서 주로 써요.

phrases.en: I walked through the metal detector at the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨은 것을 찾는 기계를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a machine that finds hidden things.

phrases.example: 탐지 장치가 고장 나서 경보가 울리지 않았어요.
phrases.en: The detection device broke, so the alarm didn't sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찾아내는 기능을 가진 장치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a device that has a detecting function.

phrases.en: Dogs have an excellent ability to detect smells.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨은 것을 찾아내는 힘을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the ability to find hidden things.

explain_en: 발견 is finding something in general; 탐지 is searching for something hidden on purpose with a device or tool. That is why it appears with machine terms like 연기 탐지 (smoke detection) and 금속 탐지 (metal detection). It is used more in news, tech and science than in casual talk.

t90.ax: I took a lie detector test.

en: to be expanded; to be enlarged; to be increased

examples.en: When you tap the photo, the screen zooms in.
The scale of the business grew a lot this year.
It is easy to read because the letters are enlarged.
Support will be extended to young people too.
The child laughed at the picture getting bigger.
I'll tell you before the problem gets bigger.

explain: 크기나 범위가 커질 때 써요. 반대말은 '축소되다'예요. 사람이 크게 만들면 '확대하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Please enlarge the photo and look at it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 크게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person makes something larger.

phrases.en: The problem is gradually getting bigger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 커지는 중이라는 뜻의 진행형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A progressive form meaning it is growing bit by bit.

phrases.en: The screen shrinks smaller.
phrases.nuance_ko: '확대되다'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '확대되다'.

explain_en: Use it when size or range grows. The opposite is '축소되다'. When a person enlarges something, use '확대하다'.

dis.h: scale or scope gets bigger, like photos
gh: swell in volume, like gas or economy

p.n: 확대 means the scale grows; 확장 means the market reaches farther.

examples.en: I went to the hospital to get tested for hepatitis.

examples.ko: 간염은 예방 주사로 막을 수 있는 경우가 있어요.
examples.en: Some kinds of hepatitis can be prevented with a vaccine.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 간염을 앓았지만 지금은 괜찮아요.
examples.en: I had hepatitis as a child, but I'm fine now.

examples.ko: 간염에 걸리면 피로감이 심할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you get hepatitis, you can feel very tired.

examples.ko: 가족 중에 간염 환자가 있어서 조심해요.
examples.en: There's a hepatitis patient in my family, so I'm careful.
At the health checkup I was told hepatitis was suspected.

explain: 보통 'B형 간염'처럼 종류 이름과 함께 나와요. '간염에 걸리다', '간염을 앓다'처럼 말하고, 건강검진 이야기에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I got the hepatitis B vaccine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간염의 종류를 말할 때 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to name a type of hepatitis.

phrases.en: I heard he caught hepatitis because he wasn't careful about food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 감염된다는 뜻으로 '병에 걸리다' 형태로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting infected, using the '병에 걸리다' pattern.

phrases.example: 간염 예방을 위해 손을 자주 씻어요.
phrases.en: I wash my hands often to prevent hepatitis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병을 막는 일을 말할 때 '예방'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 예방 refers to preventing the disease.

explain_en: It usually comes with a type name, as in 'B형 간염' (hepatitis B). People say '간염에 걸리다' or '간염을 앓다', and you often hear it when talking about health checkups.
